anomalies.observed: The MAX3485's differential outputs A (pin 6) and B (pin 7) both carry the same net label 'TTL', placing them on one net and shorting the differential pair together.
anomalies.expected: A and B are the differential pair of the RS-485 transceiver; for the single-wire servo bus only one of them should drive the bus, and the two must not be shorted.

evidence.quote: U1 pin 6 (A) and pin 7 (B) both labelled 'TTL'
Bias/pull network on the MAX3485 A/B differential lines and DE/RE enable line

anomalies.impact: Shorting A and B prevents the transceiver from producing a valid single-ended/differential signal, so serial-mode servos would not communicate.

parsed.summary: The MAX3485's A and B pins are both tied to the same 'TTL' net, shorting the differential pair; this would prevent serial-mode servo communication. Confidence is limited because the spec's 'shared single-wire TTL serial bus' wording could be read as intending a single-wire node.
